The main takeaway from our work is that

the proper form of an information criterion for mixture cure models is the one that is based on a log-likelihood that is the difference between the log-likelihood of the complete data and the log-likelihood under the null hypothesis that the mixture components have the same parameters.

the AIC for mixture cure models is different than the usual AIC for mixture models and that the proper form of this criterion can be obtained by using the expected log-likelihood of the observed data and not the complete-data log-likelihood.
the Akaike criterion should not be applied to mixture cure models as it is often done.
